title: System Backup Pre-flight Checker
spec: Write a script `backup_preflight.sh` to validate backup parameters. It takes three positional arguments: source_dir, dest_dir, and backup_name. Evaluate the following rules in order, printing a specific error and exiting with 1 if a check fails. If source_dir is missing, print 'Missing source'. If source_dir is not an existing directory, print 'Invalid source directory'. If source_dir is not readable, print 'Source unreadable'. If dest_dir is missing, print 'Missing destination'. If dest_dir is not an existing directory, print 'Invalid dest directory'. If dest_dir is not writable, print 'Destination unwritable'. If backup_name is missing, print 'Missing backup name'. Next, check if the environment variable `BACKUP_USER` is empty; if so, print 'BACKUP_USER not set'. Finally, if the file `/tmp/backup.lock` exists, print 'Backup already in progress'. If all pass, print 'Pre-flight OK' and exit 0.

title: User Account Provisioning Validator
spec: Write a script `validate_user_env.sh` that accepts a username and a shell path. Validate inputs sequentially, exiting with 1 and printing an exact message upon the first failure. If username is empty, print 'No username'. If the user config file `/etc/users/$1.conf` exists, print 'User exists'. If shell path is empty, print 'No shell'. If shell path is not executable, print 'Invalid shell'. If the script is not run by root (check if EUID does not equal 0 using standard integer comparison), print 'Must be root'. If the `SKEL_DIR` environment variable is empty, print 'Skel var missing'. If the directory specified by `SKEL_DIR` does not exist, print 'Skel missing'. If it is not readable, print 'Skel unreadable'. If all validations succeed, output 'Ready to provision' and exit 0.

title: CI/CD Build Environment Checker
spec: Write a function `check_build_env()` that takes a project path and a build type ('debug' or 'release'). Perform a series of checks, returning 1 with a specific error if any fail. If the project path is empty, echo 'Path required'. If the project path is not a directory, echo 'Path not a directory'. If a `Makefile` is not found as a regular file in the project path, echo 'Makefile missing'. If the `Makefile` is not readable, echo 'Makefile unreadable'. If the build type is empty, echo 'Type missing'. If the build type equals 'test', echo 'Test builds disabled'. If the `CC` environment variable is empty, echo 'Compiler not set'. If the directory `/tmp/build_out` does not exist, echo 'Output missing'. If `/tmp/build_out` is not writable, echo 'Output unwritable'. If the file `build.lock` exists in the current directory, echo 'Build locked'. Return 0 if successful.

title: Log Rotation Utility Validator
spec: Write a script `validate_log_rotation.sh` that validates parameters for a log rotation tool. It accepts a log file path and a max size in megabytes. Evaluate conditions one by one, exiting with status 1 on failure. If the log file path is empty, output 'Log path empty'. If the log file does not exist, output 'Log file missing'. If the log file is not a regular file, output 'Not a regular file'. If the log file is not writable, output 'Log file unwritable'. If the max size argument is missing, output 'Size missing'. If the max size is less than 1 (using integer comparison), output 'Size too small'. If the `/var/log/archive` directory does not exist, output 'Archive dir missing'. If the archive directory is not writable, output 'Archive unwritable'. On success, output 'Validation passed' and exit 0.

title: Web Server Configuration Pre-check
spec: Write a script `check_web_config.sh` taking a config file path and a document root path. Validate them sequentially, printing an error and exiting with 2 on failure. If the config file path is empty, print 'Config path missing'. If the config file is not a regular file, print 'Config not found'. If the config file is not readable, print 'Config unreadable'. If the document root path is empty, print 'Doc root missing'. If the document root is not a directory, print 'Doc root invalid'. If the document root is not readable, print 'Doc root unreadable'. Check if `SSL_CERT_PATH` is set in the environment; if empty, print 'SSL cert missing'. If the file pointed to by `SSL_CERT_PATH` is not readable, print 'SSL cert unreadable'. If all clear, print 'Config OK' and exit 0.

title: Service Daemon Health Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess_daemon_health()` that monitors a hypothetical service. It accepts a PID file path and a log file path. Perform sequential checks, echoing an error and returning 1 on the first failure. If the PID file path is empty, echo 'PID path not provided'. If the PID file does not exist, echo 'Service stopped'. If the PID file is not readable, echo 'PID file unreadable'. If the log file path is empty, echo 'Log path not provided'. If the log file does not exist, echo 'Log missing'. If the log file size is 0 (use the appropriate file test), echo 'Log is empty'. If the environment variable `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` is empty, echo 'Timeout undefined'. If the value of `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` is greater than 60, echo 'Timeout too high'. Return 0 if all is well.

title: Database Migration Pre-requisite Checker
spec: Write a script `check_db_migration.sh` that receives a schema file and a target database name. Check conditions one by one and exit 1 with a message on failure. If schema file is not provided, output 'No schema file'. If schema file does not exist, output 'Schema file missing'. If schema file is not readable, output 'Schema not readable'. If target database name is empty, output 'No database name'. If target database name equals 'system', output 'Cannot migrate system db'. If the `DB_PASSWORD` environment variable is empty, output 'No password set'. If the directory `/var/lib/migrations` does not exist, output 'Migrations dir missing'. If `/var/lib/migrations` is not writable, output 'Migrations dir unwritable'. Print 'Ready' and exit 0 otherwise.

title: File Sync Environment Validator
spec: Write a script `sync_env_check.sh` that validates parameters for remote file synchronization. It takes a local directory, a remote alias, and an SSH key file. Abort with exit code 1 and a specific error on any failure. If local directory is not provided, print 'Local dir empty'. If local directory is not an existing directory, print 'Local dir invalid'. If local directory is not readable, print 'Local dir unreadable'. If remote alias is not provided, print 'Remote alias missing'. If SSH key file is not provided, print 'Key file empty'. If SSH key file is not a regular file, print 'Key file missing'. If SSH key file is not readable, print 'Key file unreadable'. If the `SYNC_LOG` environment variable is empty, print 'Log var missing'. Output 'Sync env ok' on success.

title: Software Package Pre-installation Checks
spec: Write a function `pre_install_check()` that takes a package name and a target installation directory. Check conditions sequentially, echoing a reason and returning 1 on failure. If package name is empty, echo 'Package name required'. If target directory is empty, echo 'Target directory required'. If target directory is not an existing directory, echo 'Target is not a dir'. If target directory is not writable, echo 'Target is read-only'. If a file named `install.lock` exists in the target directory, echo 'Installation locked'. If the `PKG_CACHE` environment variable is empty, echo 'Cache not configured'. If the cache directory specified by `PKG_CACHE` does not exist, echo 'Cache missing'. If the cache directory is not readable, echo 'Cache unreadable'. Return 0 if successful.

title: Container Deployment Validator
spec: Write a script `validate_deployment.sh` that takes an image name and a deployment tag. Validate conditions one by one, exiting with 1 on the first failure. If image name is empty, output 'Image name missing'. If deployment tag is empty, output 'Tag missing'. If deployment tag equals 'latest', output 'Cannot deploy latest'. If the file `docker-compose.yml` does not exist in the current directory, output 'Compose file missing'. If `docker-compose.yml` is not readable, output 'Compose file unreadable'. If the `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable is empty, output 'Docker host not set'. If the directory `/var/log/containers` does not exist, output 'Log dir missing'. If the log directory is not writable, output 'Log dir unwritable'. On success, exit 0 and output 'Validation complete'.

title: Network Interface Config Validator
spec: Write a script `check_nic_config.sh` taking an interface name and a config file path. Perform checks sequentially, exiting with 1 and a specific error on failure. If interface name is not provided, print 'Interface missing'. If config file path is not provided, print 'Config path missing'. If config file does not exist, print 'Config file not found'. If config file is not readable, print 'Config file unreadable'. If config file is not a regular file, print 'Not a regular file'. If interface name equals 'lo', print 'Loopback not allowed'. If the directory `/etc/network` is not a directory, print 'Network dir missing'. If `/etc/network` is not writable, print 'Network dir read-only'. Output 'Interface OK' if all checks pass.

title: Machine Learning Dataset Verifier
spec: Write a function `verify_dataset()` taking a dataset directory and a metadata file path. Validate them sequentially, returning 1 with an error message on failure. If dataset directory is not provided, echo 'Dataset dir missing'. If dataset directory is not a directory, echo 'Dataset dir invalid'. If dataset directory is not readable, echo 'Dataset dir unreadable'. If metadata file is not provided, echo 'Metadata missing'. If metadata file is not a regular file, echo 'Metadata invalid'. If metadata file is not readable, echo 'Metadata unreadable'. If the `DATA_SPLIT` environment variable is empty, echo 'Data split not set'. If `DATA_SPLIT` equals 'test', echo 'Cannot verify test split'. Return 0 if successful.

title: Nightly Batch Job Pre-checker
spec: Write a script `batch_precheck.sh` that accepts a job name and an input file path. Exit with 1 and print a specific message upon the first failing check. If job name is empty, print 'No job name'. If input file path is empty, print 'No input file'. If input file does not exist, print 'Input missing'. If input file is empty (size 0), print 'Input is empty'. If input file is not readable, print 'Input unreadable'. If the `/tmp/batch` directory does not exist, print 'Batch dir missing'. If the batch directory is not writable, print 'Batch dir unwritable'. If the environment variable `MAX_THREADS` is empty, print 'Threads not configured'. Print 'Batch ready' and exit 0 otherwise.

title: Automated Certificate Renewal Validator
spec: Write a script `cert_renewal_check.sh` taking a domain name and a webroot path. Check conditions in order, exiting 1 with an error message on failure. If domain name is empty, output 'Domain missing'. If webroot path is empty, output 'Webroot missing'. If webroot is not a directory, output 'Webroot invalid'. If webroot is not writable, output 'Webroot unwritable'. If the `LETSENCRYPT_DIR` environment variable is empty, output 'LE dir missing'. If the directory specified by `LETSENCRYPT_DIR` does not exist, output 'LE dir invalid'. If a file named `renewal.lock` exists in `/var/run`, output 'Renewal in progress'. If the domain name equals 'localhost', output 'Cannot renew localhost'. On success, output 'Renewal pre-check passed'.

title: Audio Transcoding Queue Validator
spec: Write a function `validate_transcode_job()` accepting an input audio file and an output directory. Perform sequential validations, echoing an error and returning 1 on failure. If input file is missing, echo 'Input missing'. If input file does not exist, echo 'Input not found'. If input file is not readable, echo 'Input unreadable'. If input file size is 0 (use the appropriate file test), echo 'Input empty'. If output directory is missing, echo 'Output dir missing'. If output directory is not a directory, echo 'Output dir invalid'. If output directory is not writable, echo 'Output dir unwritable'. If the environment variable `FFMPEG_BIN` is empty, echo 'FFmpeg path not set'. Return 0 on success.

title: Cloud Storage Upload Pre-flight
spec: Write a script `upload_preflight.sh` that takes a file to upload and a bucket name. Evaluate conditions sequentially, exiting 1 with an error message if any fail. If file path is empty, print 'File path missing'. If file does not exist, print 'File missing'. If file is not a regular file, print 'Not a regular file'. If file is not readable, print 'File unreadable'. If bucket name is empty, print 'Bucket name missing'. If the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` environment variable is empty, print 'Access key missing'. If the `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable is empty, print 'Secret key missing'. If the file `~/.aws/config` does not exist, print 'AWS config missing'. Output 'Ready for upload' and exit 0 otherwise.

title: Vulnerability Scanner Readiness Check
spec: Write a script `scanner_ready.sh` taking a target IP and a report output directory. Validate inputs in order, printing an exact message and exiting with 1 upon failure. If target IP is empty, print 'Target IP missing'. If report directory is empty, print 'Report dir missing'. If report directory is not an existing directory, print 'Report dir invalid'. If report directory is not writable, print 'Report dir unwritable'. If a file named `scan.pid` exists in the report directory, print 'Scan already running'. If the `SCANNER_PLUGINS` environment variable is empty, print 'Plugins dir not set'. If the directory specified by `SCANNER_PLUGINS` does not exist, print 'Plugins dir missing'. If it is not readable, print 'Plugins dir unreadable'. Print 'Scanner ready' on success.

title: Game Server Startup Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess_game_server()` that takes a world name and a config file path. Perform checks sequentially, echoing a specific error and returning 1 on failure. If world name is not provided, echo 'World name empty'. If world name equals 'default', echo 'Cannot use default world'. If config file is not provided, echo 'Config empty'. If config file does not exist, echo 'Config missing'. If config file is not readable, echo 'Config unreadable'. If the `/opt/game/mods` directory does not exist, echo 'Mods dir missing'. If the mods directory is not readable, echo 'Mods dir unreadable'. If the `SERVER_RAM` variable is empty, echo 'RAM not set'. Return 0 if all pass.

title: Firmware Update Validator
spec: Write a script `check_firmware_update.sh` taking a firmware binary file and a device identifier. Validate conditions sequentially, exiting 1 with a message on failure. If binary file path is empty, output 'Binary missing'. If binary file does not exist, output 'Binary not found'. If binary file is not a regular file, output 'Binary invalid'. If binary file is not readable, output 'Binary unreadable'. If device identifier is empty, output 'Device ID missing'. If device identifier equals '0000', output 'Invalid Device ID'. If the directory `/mnt/usb` does not exist, output 'USB not mounted'. If `/mnt/usb` is not writable, output 'USB unwritable'. On success, output 'Update ready'.

title: VPN Connection Pre-check
spec: Write a script `vpn_precheck.sh` accepting a profile name and a credentials file path. Check conditions in order, exiting with 1 and a specific message if any fail. If profile name is missing, print 'Profile missing'. If credentials file is missing, print 'Credentials missing'. If credentials file does not exist, print 'Credentials not found'. If credentials file is not a regular file, print 'Credentials invalid'. If credentials file is not readable, print 'Credentials unreadable'. If the directory `/etc/openvpn` is not a directory, print 'OpenVPN dir missing'. If the `/etc/openvpn` directory is not readable, print 'OpenVPN dir unreadable'. If the `VPN_LOG_LEVEL` environment variable is empty, print 'Log level not set'. Print 'VPN ready' if all checks succeed.

title: Log Parser Initialization Check
spec: Write a function `init_log_parser()` that takes an access log file and an output summary file. Perform checks sequentially, echoing an error and returning 1 on failure. If access log is not provided, echo 'Access log missing'. If access log does not exist, echo 'Access log not found'. If access log is not readable, echo 'Access log unreadable'. If access log is empty (size 0), echo 'Access log is empty'. If output summary file is not provided, echo 'Summary file missing'. If the directory `/var/reports` does not exist, echo 'Reports dir missing'. If `/var/reports` is not writable, echo 'Reports dir unwritable'. If the `PARSER_FORMAT` environment variable is empty, echo 'Format not set'. Return 0 otherwise.

title: Cache Clearing Utility Pre-check
spec: Write a script `cache_clear_check.sh` that takes a cache directory and a user ID. Validate conditions sequentially, exiting 1 with a message on failure. If cache directory is empty, output 'Cache dir missing'. If cache directory does not exist, output 'Cache dir not found'. If cache directory is not a directory, output 'Not a directory'. If cache directory is not writable, output 'Cache dir unwritable'. If user ID is empty, output 'User ID missing'. If user ID equals 'root', output 'Cannot clear root cache'. If the `REDIS_HOST` environment variable is empty, output 'Redis host missing'. If the file `/tmp/cache.lock` exists, output 'Cache is locked'. Output 'Ready to clear' on success.

title: Code Linter Environment Assessor
spec: Write a script `lint_env_assessor.sh` taking a source directory and a rules file. Check conditions one by one, exiting with 1 and an error on failure. If source directory is not provided, print 'Source dir missing'. If source directory does not exist, print 'Source dir not found'. If source directory is not a directory, print 'Source dir invalid'. If source directory is not readable, print 'Source dir unreadable'. If rules file is not provided, print 'Rules file missing'. If rules file does not exist, print 'Rules file not found'. If rules file is not readable, print 'Rules file unreadable'. If the `LINT_STRICT` environment variable is empty, print 'Strict mode not set'. Print 'Linter ready' on success.

title: Mail Server Queue Processor Checker
spec: Write a function `check_mail_queue()` accepting a queue directory and a quarantine directory. Validate sequentially, echoing an error and returning 1 on failure. If queue directory is missing, echo 'Queue dir missing'. If queue directory does not exist, echo 'Queue dir not found'. If queue directory is not a directory, echo 'Queue dir invalid'. If queue directory is not readable, echo 'Queue dir unreadable'. If quarantine directory is missing, echo 'Quarantine dir missing'. If quarantine directory does not exist, echo 'Quarantine dir not found'. If quarantine directory is not a directory, echo 'Quarantine dir invalid'. If quarantine directory is not writable, echo 'Quarantine dir unwritable'. Return 0 if all checks pass.

title: SSL Certificate Generator Pre-check
spec: Write a script `ssl_gen_precheck.sh` that takes a private key path and a certificate signing request (CSR) path. Validate them sequentially, exiting 1 with a specific message on failure. If private key path is empty, output 'Key path missing'. If private key file does not exist, output 'Key file not found'. If private key file is not a regular file, output 'Key file invalid'. If private key file is not readable, output 'Key file unreadable'. If CSR path is empty, output 'CSR path missing'. If CSR file does not exist, output 'CSR file not found'. If CSR file is not a regular file, output 'CSR file invalid'. If CSR file is not readable, output 'CSR file unreadable'. On success, output 'SSL gen ready' and exit 0.

title: Build Artifact Cleaner
spec: Write a Bash script `clean_artifacts.sh` that removes old build artifacts. It accepts two positional arguments: a target directory and an age threshold in days. Verify that the target directory argument is provided. Check if the target directory exists. Check if the target is indeed a directory. Check that the age threshold is greater than 0. Check if the environment variable `CLEANUP_LOG` is non-empty; if so, verify that the log file's parent directory is writable. Iterate through the target directory. For each item, check if it is a regular file. Check if it is a symlink (skip if it is). Check if its size is greater than zero before processing. Example: `./clean_artifacts.sh /build/libs 7` removes files older than 7 days and outputs "Cleaned 4 files".

title: CSV Data Importer
spec: Create a Bash module `csv_importer.sh` with a function `import_csv` taking an input CSV file and an output directory. The function must verify that the input file argument is provided. Check that the CSV file is readable. Check that the output directory argument is provided. Check that the output directory exists. Check that the output directory is writable. Before processing, check if a lock file `import.lock` already exists in the output directory to prevent concurrent runs. Loop through each line (skipping the header) and extract the status column. Check if the status string equals "ACTIVE". Also, verify that the row's ID field is not empty. If all conditions are met, append the row to a `valid.csv` file. Example: `import_csv data.csv /out` produces `/out/valid.csv` containing only active rows with valid IDs.

title: Dotfile Symlink Manager
spec: Write a Bash script `link_dotfiles.sh` that symlinks configuration files from a source repository to the user's home directory. The script must check if the source directory argument is provided. Check if the source directory exists. Read an environment variable `DOTFILES_FORCE`; check if it equals "1". Iterate through items in the source directory. For each item, verify it is a regular file. Check if it is readable. In the home directory, check if a target with the same name already exists. If it does, check if it is already a symlink. Check if a backup directory `~/.backup` exists, creating it if not. If the target exists and is not a symlink, check if `DOTFILES_FORCE` equals "1" to allow overwriting. Example: `./link_dotfiles.sh ~/.dotfiles` symlinks files and reports "Linked 5 files".

title: Git Hook Pre-commit Linter
spec: Implement a Bash script `pre_commit.sh` that acts as a git pre-commit hook. The script must first verify it is running inside a git repository by checking if `.git` is a directory. Check if the environment variable `SKIP_LINT` equals "true", exiting early if so. Get the list of staged files. For each file, check if the file actually exists to handle deletions. Check if the file is executable; if so, skip it. Verify that the file size is greater than zero. Extract the file extension and check if it equals "sh". Check if the `shellcheck` command exists in the system PATH before attempting to run it. Example: running `./pre_commit.sh` on a repo with a staged script containing syntax errors will fail the commit and print the errors.

title: Image Thumbnail Generator
spec: Create a Bash script `make_thumbs.sh` that takes a source directory of images and a destination directory for thumbnails. Validate that the source directory argument is provided. Check if the source directory exists. Check if the source directory is readable. Check if the destination directory exists. Check if the `convert` utility is executable in the system path. Iterate through the files in the source directory. For each file, verify it is a regular file. Extract the extension and check if it equals "jpg". Check if a file with the same name already exists in the destination directory to avoid duplicate work. Example: `./make_thumbs.sh img/ thumbs/` generates thumbnails for all JPGs.

title: System Resource Alert Monitor
spec: Write a Bash script `res_monitor.sh` to monitor CPU usage and alert if it exceeds a threshold. Check if the threshold argument is provided. Verify the threshold argument is greater than 0. Check if a `/var/log/monitor.log` file exists. Check if the log file is writable. Check if the environment variable `ALERT_EMAIL` is non-empty. Read the current CPU load. Check if the current load is greater than the threshold. If an alert needs to be sent, check if a lockfile `/tmp/alert.lock` already exists to prevent spamming. If it exists, check if the find command's result string for checking lockfile age is not empty. Example: `./res_monitor.sh 80` logs a warning and emails if load > 80 and no recent lock exists.

title: Static Website Generator
spec: Develop a Bash script `build_site.sh` that compiles text files into HTML. Verify that the input directory argument is provided. Verify that the output directory argument is provided. Check if the input directory exists as a valid directory. Check if a template file `layout.html` exists in the current directory. Check if the template is readable. Check if the output directory exists. Check if the output directory is writable. Iterate over the input files. For each item, verify it is a regular file. Check if the file size is greater than zero. Extract the extension and check if it equals "txt". Example: `./build_site.sh content/ public/` compiles all non-empty TXT files using `layout.html`.

title: Podcast Episode Downloader
spec: Write a Bash script `sync_podcasts.sh` that takes a text file containing podcast episode URLs and a download directory. Verify the URL list file argument is provided. Verify the URL list file exists. Check if the list is a regular file. Check if the download directory exists. Check if the `wget` command is executable in the environment. Loop through the URLs in the file. For each URL, check if the URL string is not empty. Extract the filename from the URL. Check if the file already exists in the download directory. If it exists, check if the file size is greater than zero. Check if an environment variable `DRY_RUN` equals "1". Example: `./sync_podcasts.sh urls.txt /downloads` downloads missing episodes.

title: Database Snapshot Archiver
spec: Create a Bash module `db_archiver.sh` containing a function `archive_dumps`. It takes a source directory of `.sql` files and a target archive directory. The function must verify that the source directory argument is provided. Check that the source directory exists. Check that the source directory has read permissions. Check if the target directory exists. Check if the target directory is writable. Check if the `gzip` utility is executable. Iterate over the files in the source directory. For each file, check if it is a regular file. Check if its size is greater than zero. Extract the filename and check if the extension equals "sql". Check if the compressed version of the file already exists in the target directory to avoid re-compressing. Example: `archive_dumps /db/dumps /backup/archives` compresses and moves all valid SQL files.

title: Python Virtualenv Bootstrapper
spec: Implement a Bash script `setup_venv.sh` to initialize a Python virtual environment. Check if the target directory argument is provided. Check if the target directory already exists. Verify that the `python3` command is executable. Check if a `requirements.txt` file exists in the current directory. Check if the requirements file is readable. Check if the environment variable `OFFLINE_MODE` equals "true". After attempting to create the venv, check if the activation script `bin/activate` exists inside the target directory. Check if the pip installation exit code equals 0. Example: `./setup_venv.sh .venv` creates a virtual environment and installs dependencies if the requirements file is present.

title: Application Log Aggregator
spec: Write a Bash script `aggregate_logs.sh` that collects log files from worker nodes into a central directory. Verify that the base directory argument is provided. Verify that the central directory argument is provided. Check if the base directory exists. Check if the central directory exists. Check if the central directory is writable. Loop through the items in the base directory. For each item, check if it is a directory. Inside each node directory, check if a file named `app.log` exists. Check if the log file is a regular file. Check if the log file is readable. Check if the destination central log file already exists. Example: `./aggregate_logs.sh /nodes /central` copies readable `app.log` files from each node to `/central/nodeX.log`.

title: Firewall Rule Exporter
spec: Create a Bash script `export_fw.sh` to backup iptables rules. Check if the backup directory argument is provided. Check if the backup directory exists. Check if the backup directory is writable. Check if the `iptables-save` command is executable. Check if an environment variable `AUTO_COMMIT` is not empty. Run the dump to a temporary file, then check if the temporary file's size is greater than zero. Check if a previous backup file `latest.rules` exists in the backup directory. If it exists, compare the two files and check if the `diff` command exit status equals 1. Example: `./export_fw.sh /backups/firewall` creates a new backup if the rules have changed.

title: Temporary Workspace Sweeper
spec: Develop a Bash script `sweep_temp.sh` that deletes temporary files from a specific workspace. Validate that the workspace directory argument is provided. Verify that the workspace directory exists. Check if the workspace is readable. To prevent catastrophes, check if the workspace directory path equals `/` and exit if so. Check if the path equals `/tmp` and exit if so. Check if the age threshold argument is provided, and verify it is greater than 0. Loop through the files in the directory. Check if each item is a regular file. Check if the item is a symlink (skip symlinks to avoid deleting targets). Example: `./sweep_temp.sh /var/app/workspace 60` safely removes regular files older than 60 minutes.

title: Music Library Organizer
spec: Write a Bash script `organize_music.sh` to move unorganized audio files into target folders based on artist name provided via a sidecar text file. Check that the source directory argument is given. Check that the destination directory argument is given. Check if the source directory exists. Check if the destination directory exists. Check if the destination directory is writable. Loop through files in the source directory. For each file, check if it is a regular file. Extract the extension and check if it equals "mp3". Check if a corresponding `.txt` sidecar file exists. Read the artist name and check if the artist string is not empty. Check if the destination audio file already exists. Example: `./organize_music.sh /downloads /music` moves `song.mp3` to `/music/ArtistName/song.mp3`.

title: SSH Key Distributor
spec: Implement a Bash script `distribute_keys.sh` that copies a public key to a list of servers. Check if the key file argument is provided. Check if the key file exists. Check if the key file is readable. Check if the server list file exists. Check if the server list is a regular file. Check if the `ssh-copy-id` command is executable. Iterate over each line in the server list. Check if the line is not empty (ignoring blank lines). Check if the line does not equal "localhost". Attempt a ping to the server and check if the ping exit code equals 0. Check if the environment variable `VERBOSE` equals "1", echoing progress if so. Example: `./distribute_keys.sh ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub servers.txt` installs the key on all reachable servers.

title: Stale Container Cleanup
spec: Create a Bash module `container_cleanup.sh` with a function `clean_stale` that removes exited containers. Verify that the target status argument is provided. Check if the `docker` command is executable. Check if the environment variable `DOCKER_HOST` is not empty. Check if a `.dockerignore` file exists in the current directory. Check if the ignore file is readable. Fetch the list of containers. For each container, verify the extracted status string equals the provided status argument. Next, check if the container's age is greater than or equal to the minimum age argument. Check if the container name is not empty. Check if the `FORCE_CLEAN` environment variable equals "true". Example: `clean_stale exited 24` removes all containers that exited more than 24 hours ago.

title: Configuration Template Renderer
spec: Write a Bash script `render_config.sh` that replaces environment variables in a template file and writes to an output file. Verify that the template file argument is provided and non-empty. The input is a text file where each line is a provider metric containing a vendor, days, defects, cost, status, tier, origin, and shipping separated by spaces. Read the file. If the days are greater than fourteen, append the vendor to a slow log. If the days are exactly zero, append to an instant log. If the defects are greater than five, append to a quality log. If the cost is greater than one hundred thousand, append to a budget log. If the status is exactly the word bankrupt, append to a dead log. If the tier is exactly the word partner, append to a core log. If the origin is exactly the word overseas, append to an import log. If the shipping is exactly the word air, append to a fly log. Example input is fastcorp twenty zero ten active basic local road. Example output is fastcorp appended to the slow log.

title: Charity Donation Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(donations)`. The input is a text file where each line is a contribution containing a donor, amount, age, fees, campaign, anon, receipt, and method separated by spaces. Process the contributions line by line. If the amount is less than one, append the donor to a zero log. If the amount is greater than ten thousand, append to a major log. If the age is greater than three hundred sixty five, append to an old log. If the fees are greater than fifty, append to a costly log. If the campaign is exactly the word urgent, append to a rush log. If the anon is exactly the word yes, append to a secret log. If the receipt is exactly the word pending, append to a wait log. If the method is exactly the word crypto, append to a coin log. Example input is donorone zero ten zero standard no sent cash. Example output is donorone appended to the zero log.

title: Drone Flight Path Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(waypoints)`. The input is a text file where each line is a route marker containing a waypoint, altitude, battery, speed, zone, weather, camera, and signal separated by spaces. Check each marker. If the altitude is greater than four hundred, append the waypoint to a high log. If the altitude is less than zero, append to a crash log. If the battery is less than twenty, append to a charge log. If the speed is greater than fifty, append to a fast log. If the zone is exactly the word restricted, append to a nofly log. If the weather is exactly the word windy, append to a sway log. If the camera is exactly the word off, append to a blind log. If the signal is exactly the word lost, append to a home log. Example input is pointone fivehundred fifty ten open clear on strong. Example output is pointone appended to the high log.

title: Hospital Bed Assignment System
spec: Write a function `assign(patients)`. The input is a text file where each line is an admission record containing a patient, urgency, days, age, ward, isolation, insurance, and transport separated by spaces. Iterate over the records. If the urgency is greater than ten, append the patient to a critical log. If the urgency is exactly zero, append to a clear log. If the days are greater than thirty, append to a long log. If the age is less than eighteen, append to a minor log. If the ward is exactly the word surgical, append to a cut log. If the isolation is exactly the word yes, append to a solo log. If the insurance is exactly the word none, append to a finance log. If the transport is exactly the word heli, append to an air log. Example input is patientfive twelve ten thirty general no yes road. Example output is patientfive appended to the critical log.

title: Space Mission Countdown Sequencer
spec: Write a function `sequence(logfile)` that reads a log of subsystem statuses. First check if the file does not exist, and abort by printing missing. Check if the file is a directory, and abort by printing invalid. Initialize a power variable to one hundred and a state variable to green. Read each line from the file. If the line is empty, skip it. If the line equals thrusters, subtract ten from power. If the line equals lifesupport, check if power is less than fifty; if it is, print warning, otherwise print stable. If the line equals leak, set state to red. If the line equals abort, break the loop. After the loop, if power is less than zero, print fail. If state equals red, print danger. If power is greater than or equal to zero, print launch. For example, if the file contains leak and thrusters, it should print danger then launch.

title: Video Game Character Stat Processor
spec: Write a function `calculate(stats)` that accepts a file path containing equipment names. If the file lacks read permission, print an error. If the file size is zero, print empty. Set strength to ten and agility to ten. Read the file line by line. If a line is empty, ignore it. If a line equals sword, add five to strength. If a line equals shield, check if agility is less than fifteen; if it is, add two to agility, otherwise print heavy. If a line equals boots, add three to agility. If a line equals cursed, set strength to zero. After reading all lines, if strength is equal to zero, print doomed. If agility is greater than twenty, print nimble. If strength is greater than fifteen, print warrior. For example, an input of sword and sword prints warrior.

title: Factory Assembly Line Conductor
spec: Write a function `route(manifest)` that reads a file of part codes. If the manifest path is a directory, print an error. If it is not a regular file, print invalid. Set count to zero and weight to zero. Loop through the parts one by one. If a part equals engine, add fifty to weight. If a part equals chassis, add twenty to count. If weight is greater than two hundred, print overload. If a part equals paint, check if count is equal to zero; if it is, print missing, otherwise add one to count. If a part equals reject, print discarded. At the end, if weight is equal to zero, print empty. If count is greater than ten, print success. Example: an input of engine and chassis prints success.

title: Escape Room Puzzle Master
spec: Write a function `solve(clues)` that processes a file of guessed words. If the file does not exist, print none. If the file is empty, print start. Set locks to three and time to sixty. For each guess in the file: if the guess is empty, skip it. If the guess equals key, subtract one from locks. If the guess equals trap, subtract ten from time. If the guess equals hint, check if time is greater than thirty; if it is, subtract five from time, otherwise print notime. If the guess equals reset, set locks to three. At the end, if time is less than or equal to zero, print failed. If locks is equal to zero, print escaped. If locks is greater than zero, print trapped. Example: three lines of key prints escaped.

title: Magic Potion Recipe Brewer
spec: Write a function `brew(ingredients)` that reads lines of recipe components. If the file lacks read access, print forbidden. If the file is a directory, print mistake. Set toxicity to zero and magic to zero. Read the lines sequentially. If a line is empty, skip it. If the line equals frog, add ten to toxicity. If the line equals root, add five to magic. If the line equals crystal, check if toxicity is greater than twenty; if it is, print explosion, otherwise add one to magic. If the line equals petal, subtract five from toxicity. After the loop, if toxicity is less than zero, set toxicity to zero. If magic is greater than fifty, print wizard. If toxicity is greater than ten, print poison. Otherwise print potion. Example: an input of root prints potion.

title: Medieval Jousting Tournament Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(actions)` where the file lists actions in a joust. If the file does not exist, print absent. If the file size is zero, print forfeit. Set points to zero and armor to fifty. Read the actions line by line. If a line is empty, skip it. If a line equals strike, add ten to points. If a line equals block, add five to armor. If a line equals hit, check if armor is less than twenty; if it is, subtract ten from points, otherwise subtract five from armor. If a line equals fall, set points to zero. At the end, if points is less than zero, set points to zero. If points is greater than thirty, print champion. If armor is equal to zero, print defeated. Example: four lines of strike prints champion.

title: Submarine Dive Director
spec: Write a function `dive(commands)` to process navigation commands for a submarine. If the file is not a regular file, print error. If it cannot be read, print blind. Set depth to zero and oxygen to one hundred. Read each line. If a line is empty, ignore it. If the line equals down, add fifty to depth. If the line equals up, subtract fifty from depth. If the line equals vent, check if depth is less than ten; if it is, add twenty to oxygen, otherwise print toodeep. If the line equals leak, subtract thirty from oxygen. At the end, if depth is greater than two hundred, print crush. If oxygen is less than or equal to zero, print suffocate. If depth is equal to zero, print surfaced. Example: an input of down and down leaves depth at one hundred.

title: Mountain Climbing Expedition Guide
spec: Write a function `climb(trail)` that reads a file of trail events. If the trail file does not exist, print lost. If it is a directory, print map. Set altitude to zero and stamina to fifty. For each event line: if empty, skip it. If the event equals hike, add ten to altitude. If the event equals rest, add five to stamina. If the event equals storm, check if altitude is greater than one hundred; if it is, subtract twenty from stamina, otherwise subtract five from stamina. If the event equals cliff, subtract ten from stamina. At the end, if stamina is less than or equal to zero, print exhausted. If altitude is greater than two hundred, print summit. Otherwise print basecamp. Example: an input of hike prints basecamp.

title: Pirate Ship Navigation Compass
spec: Write a function `navigate(headings)` processing a file of steering commands. If the file is missing, print adrift. If the file is empty, print anchored. Set distance to zero and mutiny to zero. Read commands line by line. If empty, skip it. If the command equals sail, add twenty to distance. If the command equals row, add five to distance. If the command equals storm, check if distance is greater than fifty; if it is, add one to mutiny, otherwise print safe. If the command equals calm, subtract one from mutiny. At the end, if mutiny is greater than three, print overthrown. If distance is greater than one hundred, print treasure. If mutiny is less than zero, set mutiny to zero. Example: an input of sail prints nothing until the end, then prints nothing special if distance is twenty.

title: Haunted House Scare Triggers
spec: Write a function `scare(guests)` handling a file of guest reactions. If the file is a directory, print exit. If it is not readable, print closed. Set fear to zero and battery to ten. Read reactions one by one. If empty, skip. If a reaction equals scream, add ten to fear. If a reaction equals jump, subtract one from battery. If a reaction equals run, check if battery is greater than zero; if it is, add five to fear, otherwise print stumble. If a reaction equals faint, set fear to one hundred. At the end, if battery is equal to zero, print dark. If fear is greater than fifty, print success. If fear is less than ten, print boring. Example: an input of faint prints success.

title: UFO Sighting Report Categorizer
spec: Write a function `categorize(sightings)` parsing a file of observed traits. If the file does not exist, print hoax. If the file size is zero, print nothing. Set credibility to zero and speed to zero. Read traits line by line. If empty, ignore. If a trait equals lights, add ten to credibility. If a trait equals fast, add fifty to speed. If a trait equals blurry, check if credibility is greater than five; if it is, subtract five from credibility, otherwise print ignore. If a trait equals landing, add twenty to credibility. At the end, if speed is greater than one hundred, print hyperdrive. If credibility is greater than twenty, print alien. If credibility is less than or equal to zero, print balloon. Example: an input of fast and fast prints hyperdrive.

title: Interstellar Cargo Manifest Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort(items)` evaluating a file of cargo items. If the file lacks read access, print lockdown. If it is a directory, print bay. Set weight to zero and value to zero. Read items sequentially. If empty, skip. If an item equals food, add ten to weight. If an item equals gold, add fifty to value. If an item equals fuel, check if weight is less than one hundred; if it is, add twenty to weight, otherwise print full. If an item equals junk, subtract ten from value. At the end, if value is less than zero, set value to zero. If weight is greater than two hundred, print jettison. If value is greater than one hundred, print rich. Example: gold and gold prints rich.

title: Superhero Mission Coordinator
spec: Write a function `dispatch(incidents)` that reads a file of city incidents. If the file is not a regular file, print peaceful. If it cannot be read, print jammed. Set danger to zero and heroes to five. Read incidents line by line. If empty, skip. If an incident equals robbery, add ten to danger. If an incident equals fire, subtract one from heroes. If an incident equals invasion, check if heroes is greater than two; if it is, add fifty to danger, otherwise print retreat. If an incident equals cat, subtract five from danger. At the end, if heroes is equal to zero, print doomed. If danger is greater than sixty, print avengers. If danger is less than zero, set danger to zero. Example: invasion prints nothing special if danger becomes fifty.

title: Fairy Tale Story Creator
spec: Write a function `generate(plot)` interpreting a file of plot points. If the file does not exist, print silence. If the file is empty, print end. Set magic to ten and danger to zero. Read plot points. If empty, skip. If a point equals fairy, add twenty to magic. If a point equals dragon, add thirty to danger. If a point equals sword, check if magic is greater than fifteen; if it is, subtract ten from danger, otherwise print rusty. If a point equals curse, set magic to zero. At the end, if magic is equal to zero, print tragedy. If danger is greater than twenty, print epic. If magic is greater than danger, print happy. Example: an input of fairy prints happy.

title: Mars Rover Sample Collector
spec: Write a function `collect(samples)` analyzing a file of terrain types. If the file is a directory, print base. If the file is not readable, print dust. Set soil to zero and rock to zero. Read terrain types line by line. If empty, ignore. If a type equals sand, add five to soil. If a type equals quartz, add ten to rock. If a type equals ice, check if rock is greater than zero; if it is, add twenty to soil, otherwise print frozen. If a type equals void, subtract five from soil. At the end, if soil is less than zero, set soil to zero. If rock is greater than thirty, print heavy. If soil is greater than fifty, print discovery. Example: sand and sand leaves soil at ten.

title: Deep Sea Exploration Diver
spec: Write a function `explore(sonar)` processing a file of sonar pings. If the file does not exist, print surface. If the file size is zero, print quiet. Set depth to zero and fauna to zero. Read pings sequentially. If empty, skip. If a ping equals trench, add fifty to depth. If a ping equals whale, add ten to fauna. If a ping equals squid, check if depth is greater than one hundred; if it is, add twenty to fauna, otherwise print shallow. If a ping equals net, subtract five from fauna. At the end, if fauna is less than zero, set fauna to zero. If depth is greater than two hundred, print abyss. If fauna is greater than thirty, print aquarium. Example: whale and whale makes fauna twenty.

title: Lunar Colony Power Grid
spec: Write a function `regulate(panels)` monitoring a file of panel statuses. If the file lacks read permission, print offline. If it is a directory, print hub. Set power to zero and heat to zero. Read statuses line by line. If empty, skip. If a status equals sun, add twenty to power. If a status equals shade, subtract ten from power. If a status equals flare, check if heat is less than fifty; if it is, add thirty to heat, otherwise print shielded. If a status equals dust, add ten to heat. At the end, if power is less than zero, set power to zero. If heat is greater than eighty, print meltdown. If power is greater than one hundred, print optimal. Example: an input of sun makes power twenty.

title: Vintage Arcade Coin Acceptor
spec: Write a function `play(coins)` reading a file of inserted items. If the file is not a regular file, print error. If the file is empty, print insert. Set credits to zero and jams to zero. Read items one by one. If empty, skip. If an item equals quarter, add one to credits. If an item equals token, add two to credits. If an item equals slug, check if jams is less than three; if it is, add one to jams, otherwise print reject. If an item equals button, subtract one from credits. At the end, if credits is less than zero, set credits to zero. If jams is equal to three, print broken. If credits is greater than ten, print highscore. Example: token leaves credits at two.

title: Time Travel Paradox Preventer
spec: Write a function `travel(events)` tracking a file of timeline changes. If the file does not exist, print void. If the file is a directory, print nexus. Set ripples to zero and energy to one hundred. Read events line by line. If empty, skip. If an event equals meet, add twenty to ripples. If an event equals change, add fifty to ripples. If an event equals fix, check if energy is greater than ten; if it is, subtract thirty from ripples, otherwise print fizzle. If an event equals leap, subtract twenty from energy. At the end, if ripples is less than zero, set ripples to zero. If ripples is greater than eighty, print paradox. If energy is less than or equal to zero, print stranded. Example: leap and leap leaves energy at sixty.

title: Zombie Apocalypse Survival Strategist
spec: Write a function `survive(supplies)` evaluating a file of scavenged goods. If the file is missing, print starving. If the file size is zero, print barren. Set food to ten and ammo to zero. Read goods line by line. If empty, skip. If a good equals can, add five to food. If a good equals bullet, add ten to ammo. If a good equals zombie, check if ammo is greater than zero; if it is, subtract five from ammo, otherwise print bite. If a good equals bandit, subtract ten from food. At the end, if food is less than zero, set food to zero. If food is equal to zero, print perished. If ammo is greater than thirty, print warlord. Example: an input of can prints nothing special if food is fifteen.

title: Dinosaur Fossil Bone Assembler
spec: Write a function `assemble(bones)` reading a file of excavated bones. If the file lacks read access, print buried. If it is a directory, print museum. Set skull to zero and ribs to zero. Read bones. If empty, ignore. If a bone equals tooth, add one to skull. If a bone equals spine, add ten to ribs. If a bone equals tail, check if ribs is greater than twenty; if it is, add five to ribs, otherwise print fragile. If a bone equals broken, subtract two from ribs. At the end, if ribs is less than zero, set ribs to zero. If skull is greater than fifty, print rex. If ribs is equal to zero, print incomplete. Example: tooth prints incomplete.

title: Secret Agent Gadget Calibrator
spec: Write a function `calibrate(tests)` parsing a file of test results. If the file is not a regular file, print classified. If it is empty, print untested. Set stealth to ten and lasers to zero. Read results one by one. If empty, skip. If a result equals shadow, add twenty to stealth. If a result equals flash, add ten to lasers. If a result equals bang, check if stealth is greater than five; if it is, subtract ten from stealth, otherwise print loud. If a result equals water, set lasers to zero. At the end, if stealth is less than zero, set stealth to zero. If lasers is greater than twenty, print lethal. If stealth is greater than thirty, print ghost. Example: an input of shadow prints ghost.

title: Carnival Game Prize Dispenser
spec: Write a function `award(throws)` scoring a file of ring tosses. If the file does not exist, print closed. If the file is a directory, print tent. Set points to zero and fouls to zero. Read throws line by line. If empty, skip. If a throw equals bottle, add ten to points. If a throw equals peg, add fifty to points. If a throw equals miss, check if points is greater than zero; if it is, subtract five from points, otherwise print zero. If a throw equals line, add one to fouls. At the end, if points is less than zero, set points to zero. If fouls is greater than three, print disqualified. If points is greater than one hundred, print giantbear. Example: an input of bottle leaves points at ten.

title: Ski Resort Lift Operator
spec: Write a function `operate(riders)` managing a file of skier passes. If the file is missing, print blizzard. If it lacks read access, print frozen. Set adults to zero and kids to zero. Read passes sequentially. If empty, skip. If a pass equals full, add one to adults. If a pass equals half, add one to kids. If a pass equals fake, check if adults is greater than zero; if it is, subtract one from adults, otherwise print police. If a pass equals vip, add ten to adults. At the end, if adults is less than zero, set adults to zero. If kids is greater than twenty, print school. If adults is greater than fifty, print crowded. Example: full leaves adults at one.

title: Virtual Pet Care Simulator
spec: Write a function `care(actions)` executing a file of pet interactions. If the file is not a regular file, print error. If the file size is zero, print lonely. Set hunger to fifty and happiness to fifty. Read actions line by line. If empty, ignore. If an action equals feed, subtract twenty from hunger. If an action equals play, add ten to happiness. If an action equals ignore, check if happiness is greater than ten; if it is, subtract twenty from happiness, otherwise print whine. If an action equals scold, set happiness to zero. At the end, if hunger is less than zero, set hunger to zero. If hunger is greater than eighty, print sick. If happiness is greater than eighty, print joyful. Example: an input of feed leaves hunger at thirty.

title: Command Line Bookmark Manager
spec: The entry function organize(inputs) manages local text bookmarks. First, verify the user data directory exists and check if the primary bookmark file is a regular file. Evaluate if the alias argument is completely empty, and independently evaluate if the target link argument is empty. Before saving, check if the backup directory is writable and verify that a synchronization lock file is strictly absent. Finally, ensure the global configuration file is readable to apply custom formatting, and verify the user is not running the script as the root administrator.

title: Daily Journal Compiler
spec: The entry function journal(arguments) initializes a daily writing workspace. Verify the target year directory exists, and check if the month directory exists to create it if needed. Check if the daily entry file is already a regular file to avoid overwriting, and ensure the template file is readable. Evaluate if the editor environment variable is empty, and check if the provided day argument is a valid positive number. Finally, check if the offline archive directory is writable before saving a backup, and verify the session lock file is absent.

title: Shell Alias Synchronizer
spec: The entry function synchronize(options) parses a source file to update command shortcuts. Verify the source file is a regular file and ensure it is currently readable. Verify the target configuration directory exists, and check if the target configuration file is writable. Evaluate if the shortcut name parameter is empty, and independently evaluate if the command string parameter is empty. Check if the interactive prompt flag is enabled, and verify the backup directory exists to save previous states.

title: Markdown Notes Indexer
spec: The entry function index(arguments) builds a table of contents for a folder of notes. Verify the provided path is a valid directory and check if it is actively readable. Verify the output index file is writable, and check if the metadata extraction utility is executable. Evaluate if the document title parameter is empty, and evaluate if the quiet mode flag is enabled to suppress terminal output. Verify the temporary processing directory exists, and check if the final output string is completely empty before writing.

title: Desktop Font Installer
spec: The entry function install(files) processes and copies a target typography file. Verify the target file is a regular file, and check if the local user typography directory already exists. Evaluate if the user is running as the root administrator, and verify the system typography directory exists for global installation. Verify the cache utility is executable on the system, and evaluate if the target destination file already exists to prevent duplicate work. Check if the verbose logging flag is enabled, and evaluate if the provided category parameter is completely empty.

title: Video Clip Audio Extractor
spec: The entry function extract(options) strips soundtracks from media clips. Verify the input media is a regular file and check if the input file is actively readable. Verify the media conversion utility is executable on the system, and check if the input file size is greater than zero. Evaluate if the output destination directory is writable, and evaluate if the output filename parameter is empty. Check if the force overwrite flag is enabled, and verify the temporary audio workspace directory exists.

title: Virtual Workspace Manager
spec: The entry function workspace(options) moves windows between virtual desktop screens. Verify the window manager control utility is executable, and check if the target workspace number is a valid positive integer. Evaluate if the window identifier parameter is empty, and check if the user configuration file is readable to load custom rules. Verify the layout save file is writable, and evaluate if the focus immediate flag is set to switch views instantly. Check if the active display server variable is present, and verify the logging directory exists to record window movements.

title: Encrypted Password Vault
spec: The entry function vault(arguments) decrypts or encrypts text secrets. Verify the main vault directory exists, and check if the local cryptography utility is executable. Evaluate if the key identifier parameter is empty, and verify the requested encrypted file is a regular file. Check if the target file is readable, and evaluate if the terminal clipboard utility is executable to copy passwords. Check if the visual output flag is enabled, and verify the backup destination directory is writable before making changes.

title: Network Hosts Blocker
spec: The entry function blocker(options) appends blocked domain lists to the system routing file. Verify the user is running as the root administrator, and check if the system routing file is writable. Verify the download utility is executable, and evaluate if the remote source link parameter is completely empty. Check if the temporary downloaded file is a regular file, and evaluate if the downloaded file size is greater than zero bytes. Check if the backup copy of the routing file exists, and verify the network service restart utility is executable.

title: Browser Extension Packager
spec: The entry function package(directory) bundles web development files into an archive. Verify the source directory exists, and check if the source directory is actively readable. Verify the configuration manifest is a regular file, and evaluate if the compression utility is executable. Check if the graphics folder exists within the project, and evaluate if the version string parameter is empty. Verify the output destination directory is writable, and check if the clean workspace flag is enabled to remove old builds.

title: Offline Dictionary Lookup
spec: The entry function lookup(arguments) searches definitions in a local database. Evaluate if the search query parameter is empty, and check if the language code parameter is empty. Verify the database dictionary file is a regular file, and check if the database file is readable. Verify the search utility is executable, and evaluate if the formatting flag is set to print rich text. Verify the user history file is writable to record the search, and check if the phonetic spelling flag is enabled.

title: Sandbox Modifications Compiler
spec: The entry function compile(options) assembles modifications for a local sandbox game. Verify the core game directory exists, and check if the modifications folder is actively readable. Verify the configuration directory exists, and evaluate if the platform version parameter is entirely empty. Check if the java runtime utility is executable, and verify the output archive file is writable. Evaluate if the memory allocation parameter is empty, and check if the skip validation flag is enabled to bypass compatibility checks.

title: Appearance Profile Switcher
spec: The entry function theme(name) applies styles to the desktop environment. Evaluate if the style name parameter is completely empty, and verify the target style directory exists. Check if the central appearance configuration file is writable, and verify the window manager configuration is writable. Check if the icon pack directory is readable, and evaluate if the apply instantly flag is enabled. Verify the backup directory exists to save previous configurations, and check if the interface restart utility is executable.

title: Shell Snippet Loader
spec: The entry function snippet(arguments) sources custom functions into the active terminal. Verify the central snippet directory exists, and evaluate if the fragment name parameter is entirely empty. Check if the target fragment is a regular file, and verify the fragment file is readable. Evaluate if the interactive terminal flag is set before applying visual changes, and check if the local cache directory is writable. Verify the system wide configuration directory exists, and evaluate if the global apply flag is enabled.

title: Media Metadata Parser
spec: The entry function metadata(options) updates tags for local audio files. Verify the target audio file is a regular file, and check if the target file is writable. Evaluate if the tagging utility is executable, and evaluate if the quiet execution flag is enabled to suppress progress bars. Check if the release year parameter is empty, and evaluate if the genre parameter is empty. Verify the album artwork image is a regular file, and check if the artwork image is readable.

title: Raw Image Processor
spec: The entry function process(arguments) handles the conversion queue for digital camera files. Verify the source image directory exists, and check if the source directory is actively readable. Verify the destination output directory is writable, and check if the image conversion utility is executable. Evaluate if the white balance parameter is empty, and evaluate if the exposure compensation parameter is completely empty. Check if the dry run flag is enabled to simulate the process, and verify the processing log file is writable.

title: Local Environment Switcher
spec: The entry function environment(options) toggles the state of local development routing rules. Evaluate if the target environment name is empty, and verify the specific environment configuration file is a regular file. Check if the configuration file is readable, and verify the user is operating as the root administrator. Check if the system routing file is writable, and evaluate if the teardown flag is enabled to remove all rules. Verify the local server utility is executable, and check if the status log file is writable.

title: Command Line Pomodoro
spec: The entry function pomodoro(options) manages terminal based focus time sessions. Evaluate if the work duration parameter is empty, and independently evaluate if the break duration parameter is empty. Verify the notification utility is executable to send alerts, and check if the active session lock file is already present. Check if the alarm sound file is a regular file, and verify the alarm sound file is readable. Evaluate if the current task description parameter is empty, and verify the session history log file is writable.

title: Markdown Blog Publisher
spec: The entry function publish(options) moves draft posts to a live folder and rebuilds a site. Verify the drafts directory exists, and check if the drafts directory is actively readable. Verify the live posts directory is writable, and check if the target post is a regular file. Evaluate if the publication date parameter is completely empty, and verify the site generation utility is executable. Check if the repository commit flag is enabled, and verify the deployment log file is writable.

title: Terminal Task Manager
spec: The entry function todo(arguments) adds or removes entries in a simple pending items list. Verify the main task list file is a regular file, and check if the task list file is currently readable. Verify the task list file is writable, and check if the completed items archive file is writable. Evaluate if the task description parameter is empty, and evaluate if the priority level parameter is completely empty. Check if the numeric item identifier is provided when deleting, and evaluate if the mark completed flag is enabled.

title: Secure Shell Configurator
spec: The entry function sshconfig(options) writes connection blocks to the network configuration file. Evaluate if the short alias parameter is empty, and independently evaluate if the target hostname parameter is empty. Verify the identity key file is a regular file, and check if the identity key file is actively readable. Verify the user configuration directory exists, and check if the main configuration file is writable. Evaluate if the backup creation flag is enabled, and verify the system wide backup directory is writable.

title: Text to Document Converter
